newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson sees delay in market recovery.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson sees delay in market recovery.

text.p: SGS-Thomson Microelectonics NV chief economist Jean-Philippe Dauvin said it was likely that the recovery of the semiconductor market would be postponed until the second half of 1997 and real growth would only be seen in 1998 due to a slowdown in inventory buildup.
Dauvin said that legal market research bureaux were expecting a 1997 market growth ranging from 7.4 percent to 14.9 percent.
He said these forecasts had been made in October.
"They are now seeing recovery before the second half of 1997. I think they are probably optimistic. If overcapacity persists, the recovery could be postponed by one to two quarters," Dauvin said.

He said "in 1997 there will probably be a slight recovery but we will not see a big upturn until 1998. It is possible that we have to postpone the start of the recovery from June-July to the second half of 1997".
